title: The first instantiated CharacterBody3D at Vector3.ZERO, jumps on second instantiaded.
body:
### Tested versions

Tested in 4.4.1-stable



### System information

In two computers: Desktop Windows 10, Intel CPU and RTX2070. And Laptop Windows 11, AMD Ryzen7 CPU with GPU integrated.

### Issue description

When I instance a CharacterBody3D at (0,0,0) or really close to this position, and later spawn another CharacterBody3D at anywhere in the scene, the first one is moved (teleported) to the new one's position. This only happens if the first body is in so close to (0, 0, 0) and there is move_and_slide() in _physics_process(). It does not happen if the first is positioned with enough separation from (0,0,0) (eg. 0. 0.022, 2).

I'd also try to instantiate at (3, 0, 3), later move it at (0, 0, 0), and after that instantiate the second CharacterBody3D with the same result: first CharacterBody3D jumps on the new one.

The second CharacterBody3D must be instantiated in another frame that the first one. So, I'll use await get_tree().create_timer(1).timeout 

If the background overlaps the first character at their spawn time, the second CharacterBody3D does some kind of teleport from 0 to their correct position. So I've included two scenes where the ground is in another Y position.

### Steps to reproduce

You just instance a CharacterBody at (0,0,0), wait some time and instantiate second one anywhere, and the first one will teleport.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

This MRP doesn't include the "so close" values, It just spawns at Vector3.ZERO the first one and at Vector3.ONE the second one.
My tests shows that 0.021 is "so close" and 0.022 is far enouth. Also didn't try separate from world origin in more than one vector.

[jump_to_second_instanced.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20160586/jump_to_second_instanced.zip)
